description.narrative: Indian environmental NGO working with toxic material and hazardous waste through awareness building and advocacy.
Indian environmental NGO working with toxic material and hazardous waste through awareness building and advocacy.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The overall objective has been to enable a toxics free development in India along with the protection of human health. The work of Toxics Link has had impact and contributed to many developments and results in the area of toxics pollution in India.
Program areas and main results:
Toxics Free Health Care - Guidelines on mercury phase-out issued by the Central Government Health Scheme. - Guidelines on "Environmentally sound managemet of mercury from health care facilities" issued by the Central Control Board. - Government bodies of Punjab, Manipur and Kerala has taken decision and started the process to make their healthsectors mercury free. - Staff of one of the bigger hospitals trained in GuideClean Industry
Clean Industry - E-waste Rules issued by the Government of India. - Restrictions on import of second hand electronic goods introduced. - Greater aweareness among stakeholders on E-waste and growth in recycling infrastructure. - Report on the use and concerns related to Brominated Flame Retardants published and generetad wide interest among stakeholders.
Chemicals and Health - Several paint brands have phased out lead from paint. - Mandatory standard for lead in paint introduced in Sri Lanka. - Standards have been revised and improved regarding heavy metals in toys and levels of dioxin in waste plants.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
